info.title: DFOS Web Relay
info.description:
HTTP relay for the DFOS protocol. Receives, verifies, stores, and serves
identity chains, content chains, countersignatures, and content blobs.

Two data planes:
- **Proof plane** (public): signed chain operations, countersignatures
- **Content plane** (authenticated): raw content blobs gated by API-AUTH identity proofs and DFOS credentials

get.summary: Relay metadata
get.description:
Returns the relay's DID, protocol identifier, version, capabilities,
profile artifact, configured peers, and operational stats.

proof.description: Always true — a relay without proof plane is not a relay

write.description: Whether the relay accepts writes via POST /proof/v1/operations (false = lite pull-only node)

content.description: Whether the relay supports the content plane (blob upload/download; enumerate a chain's documents via GET /proof/v1/content/{contentId}/log)

log.description: Whether the global operation log is available (GET /proof/v1/log)

revocations.description: Whether the revocation status index is served (GET /revocations/v1/*)

index.description: Whether the index query family is served (GET /index/v0/*)

signing.description: Whether the optional SIGNING 0.1 mailbox courier is enabled

ingestion.description:
Admission-mode hint for POST /proof/v1/operations. `open` — anonymous
submissions admitted, subject to policy; `proof-required` — anonymous
refused at the policy step (403); `closed` — no external ingestion (501).
Absent derives from capabilities.write. Advertisement is a hint; the
relay-local admission policy is the authority.

openapi.description: OPTIONAL. URL of an OpenAPI document describing this relay's full HTTP surface — absolute, or root-relative resolved against the relay's base URL. Serving the document is SHOULD, never MUST; a relay that serves one advertises it here, and absence of the field means none is served. The document is discovery, never authority: the routes, capability gates, and auth rules the spec fixes govern regardless of what an advertised document says.

profile.description: The relay's profile artifact as a compact JWS token

peers.description: Peers this relay is configured to sync from, for mesh discovery

stats.description: Operational statistics. pendingOps is always present; the remaining fields appear when the store computes them (getStats is an optional store surface).

pendingOps.description: Count of operations pending processing (-1 if unavailable)

opCount.description: Operations this relay HOLDS in its global log. On a relay that prunes or culls, this is below the log's tip position and is not a proxy for it; counts are relay-local and not comparable across relays

countsByKind.description: Operation counts bucketed by primitive kind (all six keys present)

oldestOpAt.description: createdAt of the oldest operation in the log, or null when empty

headCid.description: CID of the newest operation in the log (the tip), or null when empty

get.summary: This OpenAPI document
get.description:
Returns the OpenAPI document describing the relay's HTTP surface. Relay
meta, ungated exactly as the well-known is — no capability flag stands
between a client and the description of the surface it is about to call.
Registered when the deployment is configured with a document
(`createRelay({ openapi: { document } })`), and its path is the value
advertised in the well-known `openapi` field. Discovery, never
authority: the routes, capability gates, and auth rules the spec fixes
govern regardless of what this document says.

post.description: Verifies the request envelope and a deposit credential rooted at the mailbox subject, then stores ephemeral courier state by request CID.

409.description: CID already holds a different request token

429.description: Subject mailbox is at the pending-request cap

get.summary: Poll the authenticated subject's pending sign requests
get.description: Returns only the authenticated subject's unexpired, unanswered requests in oldest-first order.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque composite-key cursor from a prior page's `next`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum requests to return; values above 1000 are clamped

post.description: Verifies a canonical compact JWS over the request's exact target bytes and stores it first-write-wins.

409.description: A different response already won the slot

413.description: Response body exceeds the aggregate route limit

get.summary: Fetch request status or the response artifact
get.description: Returns the unexpired request's pending, declined, or responded state without authentication.

post.description: Idempotently marks an unexpired unanswered request declined; the request may still be answered later.

413.description: Decline body exceeds the aggregate route limit

post.description:
Accept a batch of JWS tokens — identity operations, content operations,
and countersignatures. The relay classifies, dependency-sorts,
verifies, and stores each token.

Admission is a ladder, cheapest first: structural caps (400/413), then
proof verification when an identity proof is presented (401 invalid /
503 unverifiable), then the relay-local admission policy over
(principal | anonymous) — a refusal is a request-level 403 with no
per-item results — then full per-item verification. An identity proof is
OPTIONAL here and, when presented, MUST carry `jti` (write-shaped).

401.description: An identity proof was presented and is invalid (bad signature, stale, wrong binding, missing or replayed jti)

403.description: Refused by the relay-local admission policy — request-level, no per-item results

503.description: The presenter could not be resolved, the relay has no configured authority, or the admission policy could not be evaluated (fail closed)

get.summary: Get an operation by CID

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: CIDv1 of the operation

get.summary: Get an identity chain by DID

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: DID of the identity (e.g., did:dfos:cnnnft9f8a2rn938d6nkz38r847v2kr)

200.description: Identity chain terminal state (the operation log is served by /proof/v1/identities/{did}/log)

get.summary: Resolve a did:dfos to a W3C DID Document
get.description:
Resolve a `did:dfos` identifier into a W3C DID Document, following the
DIF Universal Resolver HTTP binding. Read-only and self-certifying: the
relay serves the DID-core projection of the identity chain's verified
terminal state. A deactivated identity resolves to 200 with an empty
verification-method set and `deactivated: true`. Additive — rides the
frozen v1 surface, does not touch the wire or the proof plane.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: DID to resolve (e.g., did:dfos:cnnnft9f8a2rn938d6nkz38r847v2kr)

label.description: Human-readable label, emitted for ContentAnchor service entries. Unrecognized service types are preserved verbatim, so additional properties may appear.

404.description: No identity chain found for the DID

get.summary: Revocation status for a credential
get.description:
Read-only projection of the relay's revocation set — the same
(issuerDID, credentialCID) index credential enforcement consults. A
frozen v1 contract at the relay root on its own version clock;
revocations still enter through POST /proof/v1/operations. Every positive answer carries the full
revocation JWS so a zero-trust caller re-verifies the proof instead of
trusting the boolean. `revoked: false` is an honest known-nothing answer
— absence is NOT proof of non-revocation. Relays without the index
(capabilities.revocations: false) return 501.

parameters.name: credentialCID
parameters.description: Credential CID (CIDv1 dag-cbor + sha256, bafyrei…)

revocation.description: The full revocation JWS token — present iff revoked. Self-proving.

get.summary: Paginated feed of all revocations ingested for an issuer
get.description:
Every revocation this relay has ingested for the issuer, ordered by
credentialCID ascending and cursor-paginated. Each entry carries the full revocation JWS
(self-proving). An issuer with none returns an empty array — same honest
absence semantics as the credential route.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: Issuer DID (canonical 31-char did:dfos)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Strictly-greater credentialCID keyset cursor. It need not name a present row; an unknown value resumes at the next greater key.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

revocation.description: The full revocation JWS token — self-proving

next.description: Last row's credentialCID, or null when the page was not full

get.summary: Enumerate identity chains (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Cursor-paginated enumeration of identity chains, DID ascending. A
discovery hint, never authority — every row carries the identifiers a
client needs to re-derive its claims from the frozen proof plane. The
index cannot lie by assertion (a fabricated row fails the client's
fold) but CAN lie by omission — absence of a row is not proof of
absence. The `profile` object is the single well-known projection
(profile/v1 → name): null only when the identity declares no
profile-labeled content-chain anchor; on circuit breakers the object is
kept with docSchema/name null and anchor preserved as the verification
pointer. docSchema null is an honest unknown — bytes not held, bytes
undecodable, or a document declaring no string $schema — never a claim
about what the document says.

DELETED IDENTITIES: a relay MAY omit isDeleted rows from the DISCOVERY
shapes of this route (the bare listing, the keyset and ordered walks,
nameContains, hasPublicProfile) and MUST return them, carrying
isDeleted true, from either RESOLUTION shape — did= and key=. The
presence of did= or key= makes the request a resolution whatever other
filters it carries. Relays without the capability (capabilities.index
false or absent) return 501.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: Exact DID match (zero or one row). A RESOLUTION shape: a deleted identity MUST still be returned, carrying isDeleted true.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Reverse lookup "which identities has this key ever been PROVED into". Matched byte-for-byte against the multibase public-key strings of every key-role membership a possession proof admitted across the chain's whole history — auth, assert and controller alike, not just the current head, so a key a later update rotated out still matches. A key a chain merely DECLARED, with no possession proof admitting it, never matches: that membership is void, it publishes no link between chains, and indexing it would let a stranger burn a key they do not hold by writing it into a chain. One key may match many identities. A RESOLUTION shape: a deleted identity MUST still match — key-loss recovery starts from a restored seed holding no DID, and mint-time burn checking refuses a key that already proves somewhere, so a hidden sealed row is a wrong answer rather than a thinner one. The value is opaque: a string no chain ever proved matches nothing, with no format validation and no 400.

parameters.name: hasPublicProfile
parameters.description: Boolean filter on the predicate "profile is non-null AND profile.publicRead is true" — true keeps rows where it holds, false keeps rows where it does not, absent applies no filter

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter over the projected profile name. Non-authoritative (index hint).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional author-time ordering; ordered cursors are opaque

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset cursor — returns rows with `did` strictly greater than this value (from a prior page's next). Need not be a present key; a value between keys resumes at the next greater DID.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

opCount.description: Operations stored for this chain, branch-inclusive

genesisAt.description: Author-claimed createdAt of the genesis operation

headAt.description: Author-claimed createdAt of the current head operation

profile.description: The profile/v1 → name well-known projection, or null when the identity declares no profile-labeled content-chain ContentAnchor

anchor.description: The anchored contentId — the client's verification pointer

publicRead.description: Whether a standing public-read grant currently authorizes anonymous read of the anchored chain, per this relay's fold — a hint, never an access decision

docSchema.description: $schema declared by the held head document; null when bytes are not held or not decodable

name.description: Extracted iff the held head doc declares profile/v1 and name is a non-empty string; null on any circuit breaker

next.description: Cursor for the next page (pass as `after`), or null when the page was not full

get.summary: Enumerate and filter content chains (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Cursor-paginated enumeration of content chains, contentId ascending.
Filters are ANDed exact matches. docSchema matches only chains whose
current head document bytes the relay holds and can decode — a lower
bound, not exhaustive coverage. Same hints-not-authority posture as the
identity index: verify by fetching the chain from the proof plane and
folding. Relays without the capability return 501.

parameters.name: contentId
parameters.description: Exact contentId match (zero or one row)

parameters.name: creator
parameters.description: Exact match on the chain creator (genesis signer) DID

parameters.name: signer
parameters.description: Exact DID match against accepted operation signers in the chain

parameters.name: docSchema
parameters.description: Exact opaque string match on the $schema declared by the held head document

parameters.name: publicRead
parameters.description: Filter on the standing public-read grant fold

parameters.name: documentCID
parameters.description: Exact match against currentDocumentCID

parameters.name: isDeleted
parameters.description: Exact match against terminal deletion state

parameters.name: titleContains
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match over projected title. Implicitly restricts to publicRead=true; combining with publicRead=false is 400.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional author-time ordering; ordered cursors are opaque

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset cursor — returns rows with `contentId` strictly greater than this value (from a prior page's next). Need not be a present key; a value between keys resumes at the next greater contentId.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

opCount.description: Operations stored for this chain, branch-inclusive

publicRead.description: Standing public-read grant fold — a hint, never an access decision

docSchema.description: $schema declared by the held head document; null when bytes are not held or not decodable

title.description: The public post/v1 display-name projection, null on any circuit breaker

next.description: Cursor for the next page (pass as `after`), or null when the page was not full

get.summary: Credits asserted by public head documents (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Enumerates who publicly readable post/v1 head documents say made them.
Rows are assertion-tier discovery hints derived only from held current-head
bytes; non-public, deleted, malformed, unheld, and non-post documents have
zero rows. Claim tokens and names are never projected, and hasClaim records
only string byte-presence. Rows are ordered by contentId then position.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: Exact credited DID match; malformed DIDs return 400

parameters.name: contentId
parameters.description: Exact content-chain identifier match

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Exact opaque role match; null-role rows match no role filter

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque composite cursor from a prior page's next

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when the page was not full

get.summary: Countersignatures signed by a witness (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
The reverse of GET /proof/v1/countersignatures/{cid}: every
countersignature this relay has ingested that was SIGNED BY the given
witness DID, ordered by countersignature CID ascending and
cursor-paginated. Each entry carries the full JWS — self-proving, same
posture as the issuer revocations feed. Relays without the capability
return 501.

parameters.name: witness
parameters.description: Witness DID (canonical 31-char did:dfos)

parameters.name: relation
parameters.description: Exact opaque relation match

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional recency ordering; ordered cursors are opaque

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset cursor — returns rows with countersignature `cid` strictly greater than this value (from a prior page's next). Need not be a present key; a value between keys resumes at the next greater cid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

relation.description: Open-namespace relation tag, null when omitted by the signer

next.description: Cursor for the next page (pass as `after`), or null when the page was not full

get.summary: Public credentials held by the relay (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Enumerates the relay's held PUBLIC credentials (aud "*"), filterable by
issuer and/or resource, ordered by credential CID ascending and
cursor-paginated. When the requested `resource` is a chain resource, the
`chain:*` wildcard bucket is always unioned in (a chain:* grant may
authorize the named chain). Amber and relay-asserted: the result is a
superset of candidates carrying the full self-proving JWS; the caller
folds each token against the proof plane (delegation roots at the chain
creator, revocation, expiry) before treating it as authorization — the
relay makes no authorization claim. Only public credentials are ever
stored, so targeted bearer credentials are neither enumerable nor
leakable. Relays without the capability return 501.

parameters.name: issuer
parameters.description: Issuer DID (canonical 31-char did:dfos); 400 when malformed

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Exact match against an att[].resource. For a chain resource the chain:* wildcard bucket is unioned in.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact match against an att[].action

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional recency ordering; ordered cursors are opaque

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: CID keyset cursor in lexical mode or opaque cursor in ordered mode

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

jwsToken.description: The full credential JWS — self-proving, full-fidelity att

next.description: Cursor for the next page (pass as `after`), or null when the page was not full

400.description: Malformed issuer DID, order, or cursor

get.summary: Relay-held operation recency feed (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Metadata-only browse ordering over accepted operations. createdAt is
author-claimed (credential iat normalized to ISO 8601); ingestedAt is
relay-observed. Rows never include JWS tokens or payloads. signerKey
filters by the public key the row's signature verified against at
ingest; a DID-addressed signer filter is not defined here.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Exact operation-kind match

parameters.name: chainId
parameters.description: Exact operation-log routing identifier match

parameters.name: signerKey
parameters.description: Exact multibase public-key match against the key this operation's signature verified against at ingest. Matched byte-for-byte, with no format validation: a string no accepted operation was signed with is a 200 with an empty page, never a 400. Key-addressed, not DID-addressed.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Recency ordering

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque ordered cursor from a prior page's next

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when caught up

get.summary: Enumerate standalone signed artifacts (non-authoritative index)
get.description:
Metadata-only enumeration of verified standalone artifacts. The inline
document bytes are held in the stored JWS, so docSchema coverage does
not depend on a separate blob. Rows never include the artifact payload.

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: Exact artifact CID match (zero or one row)

parameters.name: signer
parameters.description: Exact signing DID from the artifact JWS kid

parameters.name: docSchema
parameters.description: Exact opaque match on the inline document $schema

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional recency ordering; absent means lexical CID order

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: CID keyset cursor in lexical mode or opaque cursor in ordered mode

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when caught up

400.description: Invalid signer DID, order, or cursor

get.summary: Get a content chain by content ID

parameters.name: contentId
parameters.description: Content identifier (31-char hash)

200.description: Content chain terminal state (the operation log is served by /proof/v1/content/{contentId}/log)

put.description:
Upload raw bytes for a document referenced by a content chain operation.
Requires an identity proof carrying `jti` (this is a write-shaped route).
The proven DID must be the chain creator or the signer of the referenced
operation. For PUT, `ref` MUST be the operation CID whose `documentCID`
this blob satisfies.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: MUST be the CID of the content operation whose documentCID this blob satisfies

413.description: Blob body exceeds the configured maximum

get.summary: Download a content blob at a specific operation
get.description:
Download the raw bytes of the document committed by a specific operation.
The ref parameter is an operation CID within the chain. Anonymous access
is legal when a standing public-read grant authorizes it; otherwise the
creator presents an identity proof alone and a non-creator presents an
identity proof plus a DFOS read credential in `X-Credential`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Operation CID within the chain

get.summary: Download a content blob at head
get.description:
Download the raw bytes of the current document at chain head.
Anonymous access is legal when a standing public-read grant authorizes
it. Otherwise an identity proof is required (the AuthN half), and
non-creators must also present a DFOS read credential in `X-Credential`
(the AuthZ half). A read-shaped proof carries no `jti`.

X-Document-CID.description: The documentCID of the returned blob

get.summary: Paginated global log of all accepted operations
get.description:
Returns every operation the relay has accepted — across all identity and
content chains, plus countersignatures — in acceptance order.
Cursor-based pagination. Used by peer relays to background-sync. Available
only when the relay advertises the `log` capability; otherwise returns 501.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: CID cursor — start after this operation CID

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: CID to pass as `after`, or null when the page was not full

cursor.description: Deprecated alias of `next`; removed in the next minor release

get.summary: Paginated log of identity chain operations
get.description:
Returns operations belonging to this identity chain in chain order.
Cursor-based pagination.

parameters.name: did
parameters.description: DID of the identity

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: CID cursor — start after this operation CID

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: CID to pass as `after`, or null when the page was not full

cursor.description: Deprecated alias of `next`; removed in the next minor release

get.summary: Paginated log of content chain operations
get.description:
Returns operations belonging to this content chain in chain order.
Cursor-based pagination.

parameters.name: contentId
parameters.description: Content identifier (31-char hash)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: CID cursor — start after this operation CID

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: CID to pass as `after`, or null when the page was not full

cursor.description: Deprecated alias of `next`; removed in the next minor release

get.summary: Get countersignatures targeting any CID
get.description:
Countersignatures targeting any countersignable CID — operations AND
artifacts. Cursor-paginated. Returns 404 only when the CID is not a
known operation and no countersignatures target it.

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: CIDv1 of the countersigned target (operation or artifact)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor — start after this countersignature CID (from a prior page's next)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return; values above 1000 are clamped

next.description: Cursor for the next page (pass as `after`), or null on the last page

IdentityProof.description:
An API-AUTH identity proof — `Authorization: DFOS <did:dfos:identity-proof JWS>`.
The scheme token is `DFOS`, matched case-insensitively; it is deliberately
NOT `Bearer`, because nothing carried here is a bearer token. The proof
binds one exact request (method, the relay's own configured authority,
origin-form path, body hash) inside a freshness window the relay owns, and
resolves the signer's key against CURRENT identity state. On a write-shaped
route (blob upload, operation ingestion) the proof MUST also carry a `jti`
member, recorded in the relay's replay cache.

Credential.name: X-Credential
Credential.description:
A DFOS credential JWS presented in the `X-Credential` header — the AuthZ
half of the relay's split. `apiKey` is OpenAPI's honest generic type for
"a token in a named header"; nothing carried here is a bearer artifact —
the possession claim lives entirely in the identity proof this scheme is
ANDed with, and a credential without its proof authorizes nothing. The
relay serves no request-proof (`did:dfos:request-proof`) route, so this
scheme appears only in the identity-proof + credential combination.

next.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `after`, or null when the page was not full

revokedGrant.description: Revoked public grant scope; omitted when the credential was not held

dependencyMissing.description: True when rejection is retryable because a dependency is missing

headCID.description: CID of the current head operation

state.description: Verified terminal state. The three key arrays are EFFECTIVE state — the key-role memberships a possession proof admitted — so a key the chain declared but nothing ever proved does not appear in them and does not resolve. The optional declared / voidKeys / provedKeys members carry the rest of the picture; a relay MAY omit them.

declared.description: What the chain's head operation SAYS, void memberships included. Structural state — never a resolution basis.

voidKeys.description: Declared key-role memberships no possession proof admitted, and therefore absent from effective state. Empty on a fully-proved chain. Served so a controller can DISCOVER that a key they added does not resolve — a chain that verifies and a key that is not there is otherwise invisible to them. A void membership never invalidates the operation that declared it or the chain.

operationCID.description: CID of the operation whose declaration is unproved.

provedKeys.description: HAS-EVER-PROVED — the union of every effective key state this chain has held. Monotonic: a key proved into a role and later rotated out stays, because the fact it names is that possession was once demonstrated. This is the basis for verifying long-lived artifacts across a rotation, and the basis of the key= reverse index on /index/v0/identities.

services.description: Resolved discovery vocabulary (controller-signed). Each entry has a common envelope {id, type}; recognized types DfosRelay and ContentAnchor carry type-specific fields. The namespace is open — unrecognized types are preserved verbatim.

NotImplemented.description: Capability not supported by this relay
